body: We should create an interface rather than relying on the existing code inference.
If we make this API public, the options should be explicit. I'd suggest remplacing `toggleListening` by `onListenStart` and `onListenEnd`.
Does this state translate to other voice solutions? Can you copy/paste a usage with another solution so that we better understand how the API can work?
why?
toggle listening is a function to toggle the listening, not event listeners

other api didn't need isSpeechFinal since it didn't give intermediary results (only will transcribe once text is finished, and thus isSpeechFinal will be true). A fully local transcribing service would be able to use the variable though
Because it's a contract that we now need to respect internally too. It makes it obvious when we break it, and will make it easier to export.

Than perhaps `start` and `stop`.

It seems like `toggleListening` is redundant with `dispose` too, since it calls `dispose` despite `dispose` being exported too.
Do you have an external API implementation usage so we better understand?
it's not yet public, so I sent it on slack

You wouldn't write `typeof true`, but you'll explicitly write `boolean`.

Would it make sense to allow `getState` to return a custom state shape? If so, that's another limitation of this line.
dispose removes listeners, so it's different. We could expose start & stop from the helper & put toggleListening inside the connector indeed
`isListening` seems to share lots of similarities with state variables, like `isSpeechFinal`. Wdyt about having `isListening` in `getState`?
We can rename our internal functions `startListening` and `stopListening` to use the same vocabulary. Wdyt?

When we expose a value that is explicitly not defined in our codebase, we usually set it to `null` ([examples](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/1a6dc518763132eb3223c078cb38841bca83b602/src/widgets/index/index.ts#L47-L65)).

I think we should do the same here.

Our implementation for `isListening()` is 

```js
  const isListening = (): boolean =>
    state.status === 'askingPermission' ||
    state.status === 'waiting' ||
    state.status === 'recognizing';
```

For our case, we could have it as a boolean variable in `getState`.
However, in terms of using third-party helpers, `isListening` might have to be a function on their side (idk).
And `isListening, startListening, stopListening` sounds consistent to me.
https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4363/commits/9fe79ab80fd29595839a5364cd9939821ffe9d2e

I don't know what you're talking about, error code is defined in our implementation, but since we don't use it ourselves (only exposed to users, so breaking change to change that), it's either a string or undefined. This is not a scoped variable, but just some key in an object.

Do I misunderstand what you're suggesting?

In the custom helper I wrote the condition is

```js
  const isListening = () =>
    state.status === 'askingPermission' || state.status === 'recognizing';
```

since there's no 'waiting' phase. Other custom flows will have their own statuses as well
I meant that it would have made sense to have it be a `string | null` but didn't realise it's already exposed to user, so breaking change 👍
Right! I don't have a complete understanding of ways to use the voice search widget so I'm only suggesting ideas, they might not make total sense—feel free to ignore.
To make sure I understand: are these state properties necessary for all voice solutions, or only for our default implementation? In other words, should we accept unknown properties in the state?
